content.comment_body: Hello forum, I have a faulty [product_name] [version_no] model [article_no], but it is discontinued. A new version [article_no] is available. Can I install it in my [product_name] [version_no] without code modifications for the new expansion card to be accepted? Any advice would be appreciated.

Hello [user_name], Welcome to the forum. Expansion modules with order numbers ending in [article_no] are only compatible with devices of the [version_no] series. They won't work with [product_name] units or expansion modules from series [version_no] to [version_no].

Thank you for your support. Just to confirm: a) Is upgrading my [product_name] [version_no] [article_no] to the latest [product_name] [version_no] series the only way to use new expansion card versions like the [article_no] series? Sorry for so many questions—I'm not an expert in these matters. Best regards [user_name]

A new question by [user_name] was moved to a separate thread regarding whether programmed code from a [product_name] [version_no] series can be transferred to a [product_name] [version_no] and operate correctly. Best regards [user_name]
Regarding point 1: To use expansion modules with order numbers ending in [article_no], the basic device must be a [product_name] [version_no].
Thank you for your quick reply. We now understand how to move forward.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is facing challenges with hardware compatibility when replacing an obsolete module with a newer version. Uncertainty about whether the updated module will work with their existing controller, and what additional changes or upgrades may be required, highlights the need for clear documentation on hardware compatibility for successful maintenance and product updates.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes the new expansion module will be a straightforward replacement for their current system, operating with their existing setup without additional program adjustments or hardware purchases.
